questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose the University of Wisconsin–Madison because I wanted to experience a different study environment and an educational approach that is significantly different from the one I am used to in Denmark. I was motivated by the more interactive and discussion-based classroom culture, as well as the strong sense of campus life, which I believe will challenge me both academically and personally and give me a broader perspective on higher education.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: t was easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. There was a well-organized welcome, and we had a Zoom meeting shortly after arriving that provided important and helpful information. Additionally, it was easy to get in contact with the International Student Office in Madison whenever questions came up, which made the transition much smoother.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, I received support through a Zoom meeting that provided essential practical information, as well as a guided campus walk that helped us get familiar with the university and its facilities. There were also small social events at the beginning of the semester, which made it easier to meet other exchange students and feel welcomed into the community.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult to find off-campus housing, as most housing options require a full-year lease. Finding a lease for only one semester was stressful and challenging, and it required a lot of time and flexibility. My recommendation would be to start the housing search very early and, if possible, look into subleases or university-recommended housing platforms, as these can be more suitable for exchange students staying for a shorter period.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: uture exchange students should be aware that living off campus requires early planning, as most leases are for a full year and short-term options can be limited. It is important to read lease agreements carefully and be prepared for additional costs such as utilities and internet, which are not always included. Living off campus can be a great experience, but flexibility and patience are key, especially when staying for only one semester.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was different from what I was used to, as the system at the host institution works differently than in Denmark. It took some time to get used to, but once I understood the structure, the process became manageable and worked well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help was readily available through the International Student Office in Madison, who were very helpful and quick to respond to emails, both before departure and after arrival, whenever questions came up.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful in registering for the classes I wanted and was able to enroll in all the courses I had planned to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend that future exchange students stay in close contact with the International Student Office and do not hesitate to reach out by email if they have questions about registration. They are very helpful and responsive, and contacting them early can make the registration process much smoother.

questions.answer: BA

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was appropriate and well-matched to my academic background. There were many assignments and frequent quizzes for each class, which required continuous engagement, but this is part of a different educational system and teaching approach than what I am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was very different from that at UCPH, with mandatory lectures and a strong focus on continuous participation. The instructors were highly engaged, approachable, and supportive, which created a motivating and positive learning environment.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
COMARTS200: Introduction to Digital Communication
COMARTS260: Communication and Human Behavior
COMARTS266: Theory and Practice of Group Discussion
COMARTS345: Online Communication & Personal Relationships

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend COMARTS200: Introduction to Digital Communication and COMARTS345: Online Communication & Personal Relationships. Both courses had excellent instructors and were closely connected to real-world examples, which made the content easy to relate to and engaging. The assignments throughout the semester were interesting and relevant, encouraging reflection on everyday digital communication and personal experiences, which made the courses both motivating and rewarding.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: One unexpected cost was the tipping culture, as tips are expected in many situations and quickly add up. Additionally, sales tax is added to most purchases, which increased everyday expenses. I also encountered extra fees when using my Danish card abroad, which made transactions more expensive than anticipated.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were much more expensive than I expected, especially if you want to eat something other than fast food. Fresh and healthier food options in particular were significantly more costly, which made everyday grocery shopping more expensive than anticipated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a wide range of cultural, athletic, and social activities available for students. The school spirit was very strong, inclusive, and engaging, creating a strong sense of community on campus. There were many sports activities and long-standing athletic traditions, which played a big role in student life and made it easy to get involved and feel connected.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend attending sports events, especially football games and other major matches. They are a big part of campus culture and school spirit and are a great way to experience American college traditions. These events are very social, energetic, and inclusive, making them an excellent opportunity to meet other students and feel part of the campus community.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: would recommend attending football games and other sporting events to experience the strong campus spirit. Additionally, exploring the cultural life of the city is a great way to spend weekends and holidays, as Madison offers museums, local events, cafés, and a lively downtown area that reflects the city’s character and student life.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: t was relatively easy to adjust to the local culture. People were very open, welcoming, and helpful, which made it easy to feel comfortable and included. Although there were cultural differences, they were easy to adapt to and became a positive part of the exchange experience.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One cultural difference I found challenging was the tipping culture, as it is expected in many everyday situations and requires constant awareness. Additionally, the more structured and mandatory approach to classes and participation was different from what I was used to, but it became easier to adapt to over time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I especially appreciated how welcoming and approachable people were, which made it easy to feel included and at home. I also greatly valued the strong school spirit, which created a sense of community and made campus life engaging and enjoyable.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: First, I would strongly recommend contacting former exchange students, as UCPH provided very limited practical help, and insights from students who had already been there were far more useful. Second, start planning housing early, as finding short-term leases can be challenging. Third, make the most of campus life by attending classes, social events, and sports activities, as they are a big part of the exchange experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should be prepared for a more structured and demanding study system with continuous assignments and mandatory attendance, which can be different from what they are used to. At the same time, the strong campus culture, supportive instructors, and welcoming student environment make the experience very rewarding. Being proactive, flexible, and open to new experiences will greatly enhance the exchange experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was becoming part of a very welcoming and engaged campus community. Experiencing a different study culture with strong school spirit, supportive instructors, and close interaction with other students broadened my perspective both academically and personally and made the exchange experience truly memorable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was finding housing for only one semester, as most off-campus options require a full-year lease. The process was stressful and time-consuming and required a lot of flexibility and early planning.
